comparison: Perfect agreement on claims C95-C101 regarding T45L/T46L mutant data. Both OpenEval and peer reviewers support the findings that this mutant passes through the same pre-integrated intermediate but escapes arrest at longer lengths, with OpenEval rating as SUPPORTED and peer reviewers accepting these mutagenesis results.

Strong agreement on claims C102-C107 regarding systematic TMD mutagenesis. Both evaluations support the findings that TMD properties influence CT8 sensitivity in a position-dependent manner. OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED (with minor speculation noted in C108), and peer reviewers accept these systematic mutagenesis experiments without concerns.

Agreement on crosslinking data (C58-C68) showing stabilization of pre-integrated intermediate. OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED, finding the BMH crosslinking data systematic and internally consistent. Peer reviewers describe the experiments as 'elegant' and 'convincing evidence,' also rating as SUPPORTED.

Disagreement on interpretation of CT8-arrested state (C69-C72). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED, concluding the data demonstrate CT8 stabilizes a transiently occurring intermediate. Peer Reviewer 2 rates as UNCERTAIN, questioning whether the arrested state is truly physiological or represents a non-physiological state unique to cotransin presence.

Disagreement on peptidyl-tRNA identity (C53-C56). OpenEval rates crosslinking data as SUPPORTED without concerns about species identity. Peer Reviewer 4 rates as UNCERTAIN, requesting confirmation that crosslinked bands are base-labile as expected for peptidyl-tRNA.

Disagreement on cysteine scanning data (C74-C80). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED, finding the periodic crosslinking pattern and proline control convincing. Peer Reviewer 5 rates as UNCERTAIN, questioning the V41P control data interpretation and whether it adds definitive information.

Significant disagreement on resistance mutation interpretation (C110-C111, C113, C117-C119, C128-C129). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED, viewing convergence of 11 independent mutations as powerful evidence for the cotransin binding site. Peer Reviewer 6 rates as UNCERTAIN, arguing mutations could indirectly perturb the binding site through conformational changes and that the plug mutations may be prl alleles.

Disagreement on protease protection data (C41-C43). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED, finding the protease protection assay convincingly shows TMD is not membrane-protected. Peer Reviewer 1 rates as UNCERTAIN, stating the fragment identity 'seems to be based on an educated guess' and requesting demonstration that it contains the TM span and is peptidyl-tRNA.

Disagreement on NEM accessibility data (C44-C50). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED, finding NEM accessibility data consistent with other evidence that CT8 prevents TMD membrane protection. Peer Reviewer 3 rates as UNCERTAIN, noting the odd observation that C49 appears 20% more accessible with CT8 at short chain lengths, though this doesn't affect main conclusions.

OpenEval rates claims C88-C94 regarding Sec61α cysteine mapping as SUPPORTED, finding the identification of crosslinking sites provides strong spatial constraints. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these specific claims.

OpenEval rates claims C32-C33, C128-C134 regarding the mechanistic model as UNCERTAIN, noting the specific molecular mechanism is largely speculative and requires structural validation. Peer review R9 addresses only C128-C129 (resistance mutation location) but not the full mechanistic model.

OpenEval rates claims C123-C127 regarding the integrated TMD integration model as UNCERTAIN, noting significant speculation about conformational transitions. No corresponding peer review evaluation found addressing this integrated model.

OpenEval rates claims C34, C121-C122 regarding broader implications (TMD facilitating gate opening, connection to pulling forces) as UNCERTAIN, noting these are speculative interpretations for future work. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.

OpenEval rates claims C1-C28, C35-C36, C120 as SUPPORTED background/context claims from prior literature with appropriate citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found, as these represent established knowledge rather than new findings requiring peer assessment.

OpenEval rates claim C135 (citing Hizlan et al., 2012 structural finding) as SUPPORTED as appropriately attributed prior work. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for this single citation claim.
